embeds.title: 🇺🇸 Fed holds at 3.75–4.00%, two officials wanted a hike · 🟡 Mixed for markets
embeds.description:
**Decision: HOLD at 3.75%–4.00% · Forecast hold (4.00% top) · Previous 3.75%–4.00% · Vote 10–2**
The Federal Funds Rate is the rate banks charge each other overnight. The Fed (the US central bank) sets it, and it flows into every loan, mortgage and bond yield. The FOMC is the Fed committee that votes on it. Note: the chair is now Kevin Warsh (not Powell), and he gave the press conference.

fields.name: 🟢🔴 Good or bad news?
fields.value: In line on the number: a hold was fully expected after September's hike. The surprise was hawkish (hawkish = leaning toward higher rates to fight inflation). Two voters, Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed's Hammack, dissented (voted against) because they wanted another 0.25% hike now. The statement upgraded growth from "solid" to "strong" and kept "inflation remains elevated". It added: "The Committee will deliver price stability." The twist: a strong economy is good news, but it gives the Fed room to hike again. Higher rates hurt Nasdaq most. Stocks still rose, so the market read it as a calm hold, not a shock.

fields.name: 🏛️ What it means for the economy
fields.value: Growth is strong (Atlanta Fed's GDPNow estimate: about 3.4% for Q3), jobs are steady, but inflation is too high: headline CPI ran 3.7% a year in September, pushed by oil above $100. Warsh said policy is starting to work and the Fed wants "more information" before the next step. He refused to promise anything about December (no forward guidance, meaning no hints about future moves). Futures markets now lean toward one more hike in December (9 Dec), possibly more in 2027. Rate cuts look far away. Also new: from 2027, one of the eight yearly meetings will be strategy-only, with no rate vote.

fields.name: 📈 Nasdaq (NQ) & S&P (ES)
fields.value: Short term, neutral to slightly positive: no hike today, and Warsh sounded patient. The bigger headwind is the 10-year yield above 5%. The 10-year yield is what the US government pays to borrow for 10 years, and it sets the cost of money for everyone. When it rises, future tech profits are worth less today, so NQ suffers more than ES. Tonight's real driver is Big Tech earnings (Microsoft, Alphabet reported after the close), not the Fed.

fields.name: 🇯🇵 Nikkei (NKD) & yen (6J)
fields.value: 6J barely moved: USD/JPY closed flat near 157.9 (so 6J flat). A wide gap between US and Japanese rates keeps the yen weak, because money flows to where it earns more. A weak yen helps the Nikkei: exporters like Toyota earn dollars that convert into more yen. Risk: near 158, Japan may step in to support the yen. A sudden 6J jump would weigh on NKD. A December Fed hike would keep the yen soft, which supports NKD.

fields.name: 🛢️ Commodities & metals
fields.value: Gold usually dislikes higher rates (it pays no interest), but it held up, +0.4% near $4,078, helped by a softer dollar during the press conference and inflation worries. Crude (CL) is the main inflation driver: about $101.5 at the close (+1.3%), after touching ~$103.5. Expensive oil keeps the Fed hawkish. Silver tends to follow gold. Copper likes strong growth, and the Fed called growth strong, so that supports it, but higher rates are a drag over time. No Fed-specific move in hogs or grains.

fields.name: 📊 How markets actually reacted
fields.value: By the close (investingLive): S&P 500 +0.28% to 7,744. Nasdaq 100 +0.55% to 29,813. US 2-year yield −1 bp to 4.72%, 10-year +5 bp to 5.04%: the curve steepened (short rates fell, long rates rose). bp = basis point = 0.01%. Dollar slipped during the press conference, mixed on the day. USD/JPY flat at 157.94 (6J flat). Gold +0.4% (~$4,078). Crude +1.3% (~$101.5). An intraday snapshot (Yahoo) showed Nasdaq −0.2% and gold −0.6% before both recovered. Nikkei futures: no clear reaction found.

fields.name: 🧭 Bias takeaway
fields.value: The Fed gave no new push either way. It is a hawkish hold, with rates staying high and maybe one more hike in December. That is a mild headwind for NQ (watch the 10-year near 5%), a mild support for NKD while the yen stays weak, and a supportive backdrop for crude and gold while inflation is the story. Conviction is low: Big Tech earnings tonight, the US midterms (3 Nov) and the next CPI report matter more. A cooler CPI or falling oil would ease the hike talk and help NQ. Japanese action to support the yen would hit NKD.

footer.text: Sources: Federal Reserve, Yahoo Finance, investingLive. Context, not signals. Not advice.

embeds.title: 🏦 Hedge fund positioning · week to Tue 20 Oct
embeds.description:
**What this is:** every Friday the US regulator (the CFTC) publishes the **Commitments of Traders (COT)** report: who holds which futures as of the Tuesday before. We watch the **hedge funds** (called *managed money* in commodities, *leveraged funds* in indices and currencies) because they chase trends with big money.

**How to read it:** *net long* = more bets on price going up than down. The **percentile** compares today with the last 3 years: 95th = more bullish than 95% of the time. Above 90th or below 10th = a **crowded trade**: nearly everyone who wants in is already in, so there's little fuel left that way and a sharp **squeeze** the other way gets likely when price turns (losing funds rush to exit). **Commercials** are producers and users (farmers, miners, oil firms). When they sit at the opposite extreme to funds, that's the classic COT setup.

**This week's headlines:**
1. **Commodities are where the extremes are.** Hogs, natural gas and silver have funds at or near their most bearish in 3 years, with commercials heavily long: squeeze fuel.
2. **Crude and gold: funds are light**, commercials at 3-year highs. Room for funds to buy back in.
3. **Nasdaq is the one crowded long** (94th pct), and soybeans too: less fuel left upward.

Next report: Saturday about 6:30am Sydney.

fields.value:
1. **HE hogs:** funds 1st pct short, commercials 98th long. Squeeze-long setups favoured; wait for a daily SFP of the July 2024 low.
2. **NG nat gas:** funds 1st pct, almost a record short and still adding. Squeeze risk high once price stops falling.
3. **SI silver:** funds 3rd pct, commercials 94th. Long setups favoured on a daily reversal.
4. **CL crude & GC gold:** funds light (13th, 24th), commercials 94th/99th. Longs have fuel; shorts are swimming against the big players.
5. **NQ:** funds 94th pct long. Be pickier with longs; a failed high could unwind fast.
6. **ZS soybeans:** funds 94th long, commercials 17th. Short setups favoured if a daily SFP high forms.

embeds.title: 🇺🇸 US Q3 GDP & Sept Core PCE · 🟡 Mixed for markets (strong growth, sticky inflation, Fed hike risk stays)
embeds.description:
**GDP: Actual 3.4% · Forecast 3.2% · Previous 2.2% (Q2, revised; calendar showed 1.5%)**
**Core PCE m/m: Actual 0.3% · Forecast 0.3% · Previous 0.2%** (y/y 3.1%, as expected; headline PCE +0.5% m/m, 3.6% y/y)

GDP (gross domestic product) is the total value of everything the US produced, shown as an annualised growth rate. Core PCE is the Fed's favourite inflation gauge: price changes on what people buy, minus jumpy food and energy. Traders care because together they tell the Fed whether to raise, hold or cut rates.

fields.name: 🟢🔴 Good or bad news?
fields.value: Growth beat (3.4% vs 3.2%, the fastest in a year per Bloomberg), driven by consumer spending and AI investment. Inflation landed exactly as expected, but 3.1% core is still well above the Fed's 2% goal. The twist: a strong economy is good for company profits, but it gives the Fed no reason to cut and some reason to hike. Higher rates hurt richly priced tech (Nasdaq) the most.

fields.name: 🏛️ What it means for the economy
fields.value: Growth is strong, inflation is stuck around 3%, and there is no sign of the economy cooling. The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on Wednesday after hiking in September, with two members voting for another hike, and upgraded its view of the economy to 'strong'. Futures priced roughly an 81-87% chance of a December hike before this data. Nothing here argues against it. Next test: the Employment Cost Index (wage growth) on Friday.

fields.name: 📈 Nasdaq (NQ) & S&P (ES)
fields.value: Mild headwind. Strong growth supports earnings, but 'higher for longer' rates and a 10-year yield near 5% (the yield is the interest rate on 10-year government bonds) compress tech valuations. NQ was already down about 1% pre-data on a weak Alphabet report. The in-line core number removes the worst-case scare, so the data alone is not a big new sell signal. ES holds up better than NQ.

fields.name: 🇯🇵 Nikkei (NKD) & yen (6J)
fields.value: Strong US data plus Fed hike risk keeps US yields high, which supports the dollar and weighs on the yen (6J down). USD/JPY was trading near 158, so the yen is already weak. A weaker yen usually helps the Nikkei because exporters like Toyota earn more when they convert dollar sales back to yen. Watch the Bank of Japan decision due Fri 30 Oct: a surprise hike would lift 6J and hit NKD.

fields.name: 🛢️ Commodities & metals
fields.value: Gold: hurt by high rates and a firm dollar (gold pays no interest, so it loses appeal when bonds pay 5%). It slid about 1% pre-data to near $4,035. Silver follows gold but also has an industrial side. Copper and crude like strong growth, so 3.4% GDP is mildly supportive, but crude (WTI near $101) is driven more by the Middle East conflict and fell about 1-2% today. Hogs/grains: no direct link.

fields.name: 📊 How markets actually reacted
fields.value: No clear post-release reaction found yet in sources. Pre-data levels (about 7am NY): NQ -0.9% to -1.25%, ES -0.2% to -0.4%, US 10-year near 5.00%, Dollar Index 102.1 (+0.1%), gold about $4,035 (-0.4%), WTI about $101 (-1.3% to -2%). Since core PCE matched forecast, a big knee-jerk move was unlikely. Check your charts for the 8:30am NY candle.

fields.name: 🏦 Hedge funds (COT)
fields.value:
As of 20 Oct. NQ: funds net +950, 94th pct, crowded long. Hawkish rates push AGAINST it, so squeeze risk if NQ breaks lower.
6J: -22,890, 74th pct, neutral, but funds sold 30k contracts in 4 weeks. News pushes WITH that yen selling; room to run.
GC: +104,206, 24th pct, leaning short. High rates push WITH the cut-back; little fuel left to sell.
SI: 3rd pct, crowded short. Any bounce could squeeze shorts hard.

fields.name: 🧭 Bias takeaway
fields.value: Mildly bearish NQ over the next days: rates stay high and funds are crowded long, so downside moves can accelerate. Mildly bullish NKD via a weak yen, unless the BoJ surprises Friday. Gold leans soft on rates, but low fund positioning limits the downside, and silver is squeeze-prone. A soft wage (ECI) print Friday or falling yields would weaken this lean.
